image_description: Two black professional audio loudspeakers positioned against a white background. The speaker on the right is angled to show its front face, featuring a large central woofer cone and a smaller tweeter at the top, both protected by a perforated metal grille. The speaker on the left shows its side profile and partial front, revealing a similar grille pattern and branding text 'MACKIE' near the bottom. Both units have a boxy, rectangular enclosure shape with visible caster wheels at the base.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both objects clearly exhibit a rigid, rectangular box-like structure typical of speaker enclosures.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: One or more circular speaker cones on front face of varying sizes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The right speaker clearly displays a large circular woofer and a smaller circular tweeter arrangement behind the grille.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Prominent large woofer dominating the front face with a much smaller tweeter positioned above or beside it.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The spatial arrangement on the right speaker matches this description perfectly: large driver below, small driver above.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Cone surface made of paper, polypropylene, or composite with rubber surround.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Although covered by a grille, the texture and shading of the central woofer on the right speaker suggest a standard composite cone with a visible surround ring.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Grille cloth or perforated metal may cover the drivers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct perforated metal mesh pattern is clearly visible covering the entire front face of both speakers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Terminal connections visible on rear panel.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image angle shows the front and side profiles; the rear panel where terminals are located is completely occluded.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wood, MDF, or plastic enclosure with black, white, or wood-grain finish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The enclosures appear to be made of painted wood or MDF with a textured black finish, consistent with professional audio gear.
The visual features (cones, enclosure, grille) definitively identify these as electro-acoustic transducers.
The object functions as an audio output device, confirmed by its structural design.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The brand logo text ('MACKIE') appears slightly distorted and lacks the crisp edge definition of real printed vinyl decals, showing minor AI-generated character warping.

The wheels on the bottom corners lack clear mechanical definition; they appear as vague, semi-fused gray blobs rather than distinct rotating casters with axles.

alignment_reasoning: The image demonstrates near-perfect class conformance. All testable checkpoints regarding geometry, component layout (woofer/tweeter), and materials are present and accurate. The only non-testable checkpoint was the rear terminals due to viewing angle. The subject is unmistakably a loudspeaker system.

These prevent a perfect artifact score but do not detract significantly from the overall recognition.
